UnitStatement: Deliverable DEL-10-02 is named the Import/export adapter framework, in package PKG-10 (Build, Packaging, API, and Interoperability).
DEL-10-02 is type BACKEND_FEATURE_SLICE, scope item SOW-030, objective OBJ-009, context envelope L.
DEL-10-02's current production mode is setup documentation only.
The deliverable purpose is to define the framework obligations for future import/export adapters.
Anticipated artifacts for DEL-10-02 are adapter interfaces and a sample invented adapter.
The setup-run artifact boundary produces only setup documents and registers; adapter source, tests, sample adapters, manifests, and repo-level artifacts are out of write scope.
The architecture baseline is schema-first command/query/job result envelopes, JSON Schema 2020-12 contracts, and canonical JSON/JCS-compatible hashing where JSON payloads are hashed.
Adapters may translate external data but cannot bypass units, provenance, redistribution, diagnostics, private/public data controls, validation, sandboxing, envelopes, or report controls.
The external format list is TBD; concrete protected or proprietary external formats are not bundled defaults in this deliverable.
The public API transport is TBD; the public transport protocol remains a later human/product decision.
All import/export operations must be unit-aware and deterministically report unit conversions (PRD 6.6; CONTRACT OPS-K-UNIT-1).

Imported data must flag missing required fields, missing or inconsistent units, missing provenance, unclear redistribution status, protected-table risk, and user-defined reasonableness concerns (PRD 13.5).
Private rule packs, component libraries, material data, project files, and calculation results must not be transmitted or exported unexpectedly (PRD 18.2/18.3; CONTRACT OPS-K-PRIV-1).
Adapter outputs for nontrivial operations use diagnostics/result envelopes and must not make certification or compliance claims (SOFTWARE_DECOMP AB-00-06; CONTRACT OPS-K-AUTH-1).
Adapter interfaces remain code-neutral and do not bundle protected standards data or proprietary tool behavior (INIT.md; DIRECTIVE.md; IP_AND_DATA_BOUNDARY.md).
The future framework should be described as a shell around import/export providers, not as concrete bundled adapters.
Required conceptual piece: adapter identity and capability metadata.
Required conceptual piece: import and export request envelopes.
Required conceptual piece: unit-validation hooks before data enters domain workflows.
Required conceptual piece: provenance and redistribution-status validation.
Required conceptual piece: diagnostics and warning emission using project warning classes.
Required conceptual piece: private/public data boundary checks before writing exported payloads.
Required conceptual piece: rule-pack and report hooks that preserve sandboxing and report controls.
Required conceptual piece: manifest/hash hooks for reproducible imported and exported artifacts.
Reference list of governance and decomposition documents for DEL-10-02 (INIT.md, AGENTS.md, docs/*, SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md, registers, related specifications).
DEL-10-02 prepares the import/export adapter framework so later implementation can add adapters without weakening OpenPipeStress governance boundaries.
The framework is an extension surface, not a route around domain validation, unit safety, provenance, rule-pack sandboxing, reporting controls, or professional-responsibility limits.
Principle: treat adapters as translators at the edge of the application service boundary.
Principle: require schema-first envelopes for nontrivial import/export operations.
Principle: validate units and dimensional meaning before external data becomes domain data.
Principle: preserve source/provenance, redistribution status, and private/public data markings.
Principle: emit diagnostics for missing fields, missing provenance, unclear redistribution, suspected protected content, unit inconsistencies, and private-data export risk.
Principle: keep concrete format support TBD until a human decision records the external format, license posture, redistribution status, and test obligations.
Principle: use invented data only for public samples.
Parsing a file does not establish redistribution rights, engineering suitability, code compliance, or professional acceptance.
The framework should separate syntactic parse success, schema and unit validation, provenance and redistribution review, mechanics-readiness, rule-check-readiness, and human-review-needed state.
Adapters importing private material libraries, component records, rule-pack references, or project data should default to local/private handling.
Export operations should warn before writing private or protected-suspected values to shared payloads.
Trade-off (flexible ecosystem vs. governance): favor a narrow framework with mandatory validation hooks and add format-specific adapters later.
Trade-off (convenience vs. provenance): missing source or redistribution status is a finding, not an auto-filled default.
Trade-off (broad formats vs. IP safety): do not bundle protected or proprietary defaults without documented rights and human approval.
Trade-off (fast export vs. auditability): exports should carry diagnostics, hashes/manifests where applicable, and warning state.

Acceptable public sample: an invented adapter importing a small invented component record with invented dimensions, invented source metadata, and permissive redistribution marked as invented/original.

Not acceptable public sample: a bundled adapter fixture copied from a standards table, vendor catalog, commercial software example, or private project library without documented redistribution rights.

Step: route nontrivial adapter operations through schema-first command/query/job result envelopes.

The specification covers the setup definition for the future framework under DEL-10-02, establishing adapter-interface obligations, validation hooks, governance boundaries, and acceptance checks.
The specification does not implement adapter source code, sample adapters, tests, external format support, package manifests, public API transport, or repo-level artifacts.
Concrete import/export formats remain TBD; protected standards data, proprietary commercial formats, copied code tables, proprietary examples, and private user libraries are not bundled defaults.
REQ-10-02-01: the adapter framework shall operate through schema-first command/query/job result envelopes and shall not bypass the public API/plugin boundary (AB-00-03, AB-00-07).
REQ-10-02-02: every import path shall validate units before accepting external data into domain workflows (PRD 6.6; OPS-K-UNIT-1).

REQ-10-02-03: every import path shall capture source/provenance, license or redistribution status, and review disposition for records that may be contributed publicly or reused (OPS-K-IP-2; IP_AND_DATA_BOUNDARY 4).

REQ-10-02-04: imported records with missing required fields, inconsistent units, missing provenance, unclear redistribution, suspected protected origin, or out-of-range user checks shall produce diagnostics rather than silent defaults (PRD 13.5; OPS-K-DATA-2).
REQ-10-02-05: export paths shall check private/public data boundary status before writing payloads that may leave the local project context (PRD 18.3; OPS-K-PRIV-1).
REQ-10-02-06: adapter diagnostics shall include code, class, severity, source, affected object, message, remediation, and provenance when applicable (AB-00-06).
REQ-10-02-07: adapter hooks for rule packs shall preserve rule-pack sandboxing, unit awareness, versioning, checksums, and public/private status (OPS-K-RULE-1..3; AB-00-07).

REQ-10-02-08: adapter hooks for reports shall preserve report warnings, assumptions, provenance, limitations, protected-content controls, and professional-responsibility notices (OPS-K-REPORT-1/2, OPS-K-AUTH-1).

REQ-10-02-09: the framework shall not choose protected external formats, proprietary tool behavior, or specific commercial integration defaults without human approval and documented redistribution rights (IP_AND_DATA_BOUNDARY; OI-004, DEC-012).
REQ-10-02-10: the framework shall leave mechanics solve, user-rule check, and professional approval states distinct in all adapter result payloads (TYPES 4; OPS-K-AUTH-1).
No external engineering code or proprietary format standard is incorporated by this setup artifact; applicable standards are internal governance invariants.
Applicable internal governance invariants include OPS-K-IP-1/2/3, OPS-K-DATA-1/2/3, OPS-K-UNIT-1, OPS-K-RULE-1/2/3, OPS-K-PRIV-1/2, OPS-K-AUTH-1, and OPS-K-AGENT-1 through OPS-K-AGENT-4.
